page: Microsoft Azure E64d_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance features an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.6 GHz. It provides 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance integrates 504.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 7.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include support for AVX-512 instruction extensions such as AVX-512 F and VNNI, alongside dedicated AES encryption acceleration.

Storage configuration includes 2577 GB of integrated local SSD storage, suitable for temporary caches, scratch space, and swap files. The instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators, relying entirely on the host x86_64 CPU cores for processing tasks. Complementary public IPv4 addresses are not included by default.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier performance across general compute and memory-intensive evaluations. The CPU registers a PassMark score of 47,423.64 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 59,613.18, both falling within the middle 50% tier. Notably, tasks exploiting vector instructions score in the upper quartile, evidenced by a PassMark CPU extended instructions score of 58,095.88 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 254.73 GB/sec. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 180.04 GB/sec, while write operations achieve 87.34 GB/sec.

Workload testing highlights strengths in in-memory caching and transactional data processing, logging 54.07 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark database operations metric of 21,446.62. Conversely, the system is less suited for generative language model text generation due to the absence of hardware accelerators, exhibiting low token generation throughput on 135M and 7B models.

From a cost-efficiency and operational standpoint, the E64d_v4 is optimized for high-density transactional memory requirements rather than raw single-threaded execution or AI inference. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio combined with substantial local SSD space makes it suitable for large relational database engines, distributed caching nodes, memory-intensive data analytics, and enterprise enterprise resource planning backends.

Delivering 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading, the instance allocates 504.0 GB of RAM alongside 2577 GB of bundled local SSD storage. It lacks GPU acceleration, directing resources toward core compute and data-intensive tasks. Synthetic and transactional benchmarks place the server in the middle 50% for standard compute and memory bandwidth, with elevated performance in vectorized tasks like extended instruction suites and multi-threaded decompression. The instance is suitable for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caches, and enterprise data processing environments requiring large RAM allocations.
